newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - independent ECB essential for stable EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - independent ECB essential for stable EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Wednesday attacked any attempt to try to undermine the independence of Europe's future central bank saying this was an essential part of stable single currency.

In a speech to be delivered to a celebration in Bonn for the 100th anniversary of the birth of the late German minister Ludwig Erhard, Tietmeyer said there must be no doubt that the central bank had to be independent of political force.
"No one should doubt this, whatever his arguments or additional ideas," he said.

Tietmeyer's forceful statements come at a time when its European neighbour France is leading a drive to set up an informal council of ministers of those countries which join the single currency as a sort of political counterpart to the European Central Bank, which will handle monetary policy.
The Bundesbank is wary of such plans, feeling it could motivate political force which could try to an exert an influence over the central bank.
The ECB, like the Bundesbank, must have internal and not external stability as its priority, Tietmeyer said.
Stressing the need for the European central bank to have a credible policy, he said that the euro could see its stability suffer if this was not the case.

"And the hope, which I also cherish, that the euro will fluctuate less against the dollar and yen than the mark -- this hope could easily turn into the opposite," he said, according to a text of his speech released in advance.

"If the European Central Bank should be hindered in gaining the necessary credibility in markets, then the euro could easily waft to and fro on the currency markets, like reeds in the wind," he added.
He warned that even only reluctant acceptance of the need for the central bank's independence could damage the European Central Bank's credibility.
